episode.title: Try credential sources in priority order until one authenticates
episode.before: At parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, credential loading returned only the first parseable credential object. The default cached credential path preceded GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, so an expired or revoked default credential prevented the environment-provided credential from being considered. Encrypted-storage loading also returned directly, bypassing the environment-file fallback.
episode.after: At f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297, credential discovery builds an ordered list from encrypted storage or the default cache followed by GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. Authentication evaluates candidates sequentially, uses a type-appropriate client, returns the first candidate that obtains a token, and logs and continues after loading or verification failures. The explicit cloud access-token override remains ahead of the candidate list, and later interactive or compute authentication remains available if no candidate succeeds.
episode.diff: Replaced the single-result fetchCachedCredentials function with fetchCachedCredentialsList, which accumulates available credentials without stopping at the first parseable source and tolerates per-source failures. Added an ADC credential classifier, factored OAuth client construction and token-persistence callbacks into a helper, and changed initialization to verify each candidate sequentially with either GoogleAuth or OAuth2Client. Added a regression test proving that an expired default cached credential falls through to a valid GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS credential.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 is the implementation-bearing resolution for #28472, with parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7 and changes to oauth2.ts and oauth2.test.ts.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, changed_files_name_status, and git show --stat f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation returned immediately from encrypted storage or on the first parseable file in the ordered default-cache and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS paths, exposing only one credential to authentication.

The change replaces single-result credential loading with an ordered array: encrypted credentials are appended when enabled; otherwise the default cache is considered; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is then considered; malformed, unreadable, or unavailable sources are logged and skipped.
evidence_units.source: git diff c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7 f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 -- packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts, fetchCachedCredentialsList hunk

evidence_units.claim: Authentication now iterates the discovered credential list sequentially and returns only after a candidate obtains an access token; candidate verification exceptions are caught and the loop proceeds to the next candidate.

Typed non-authorized-user credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth.fromJSON, while ordinary cached OAuth credentials are applied to a fresh OAuth2Client and checked with getAccessToken followed by getTokenInfo.

OAuth client construction was centralized so every candidate OAuth client has the configured proxy and the token event handler that persists refreshed credentials and triggers post-authentication callbacks.
The exported getOauthClient entry point memoizes and invokes initOauthClient by authentication type, so the revised resolution loop governs callers using the public OAuth-client acquisition boundary.

The added regression test creates an expired default cached credential and a valid environment-file credential, makes access-token acquisition fail for the expired token, calls getOauthClient, and asserts that the environment credential is eventually applied.
evidence_units.source: git show f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297:packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.test.ts, test 'should fall back to GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS if default cached credentials are invalid or expired'

evidence_units.claim: Adjacent credential-order tests establish that a valid default cache retains priority, a missing default cache falls back to the environment file, and external-account credentials from the environment file are constructed through GoogleAuth.
The explicit configured cloud access-token override remains before cached-candidate discovery, while compute and interactive authentication paths remain after candidate exhaustion.
evidence_units.source: git diff c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7 f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 -- packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts, initOauthClient

evidence_units.claim: The repository supplies a focused unit-test oracle for source priority, missing-source fallback, credential-type adaptation, and fallback after verification failure; runtime execution results were not present in the supplied evidence bundle.

candidate_atomics.name: collect-ordered-credential-candidates
candidate_atomics.title: Collect credential candidates without stopping at the first source
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve configured credential sources into a priority-preserving candidate list while isolating source-specific read, parse, and storage failures.

semantic_action.intent: Make every configured fallback credential available to authentication while preserving source precedence.
semantic_action.pre_state: Credential sources have an established priority, but resolution returns a single credential and can therefore hide later fallbacks once an earlier source parses successfully.
semantic_action.post_state: Every successfully loaded credential is represented in priority order, and failure to load one source does not prevent later configured sources from being collected.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise valid-primary, missing-primary, invalid-source, and secondary-source cases; assert ordering and that later candidates remain reachable.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-credential-candidates-sequentially
candidate_atomics.title: Verify candidates sequentially and continue after rejection
candidate_atomics.description: Attempt each credential candidate with its appropriate authentication client, accepting the first verified candidate and treating an individual rejection as a recoverable fallback condition.

semantic_action.intent: Authenticate with the highest-priority usable credential instead of forcing reauthentication when a higher-priority cached credential is expired, revoked, or incompatible.
semantic_action.pre_state: An ordered set of credential candidates exists, but one candidate may fail token acquisition or server-side token validation.
semantic_action.post_state: The first candidate that successfully produces a usable token is returned; a failed candidate is logged and does not block verification of the next candidate.
semantic_action.validation: Make the first candidate fail token acquisition or token-info validation and make the next candidate succeed; assert that the succeeding credential is applied and returned through the public client-acquisition boundary.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-authentication-fallback-across-credential-sources
candidate_workflows.title: Restore authentication fallback across prioritized credential sources
candidate_workflows.description: Convert credential resolution from first-readable-source selection into ordered discovery followed by sequential, type-aware verification, without changing explicit overrides or downstream interactive authentication.

workflow_graph.goal: Return the highest-priority configured credential that can actually authenticate, while allowing a rejected cached credential to fall through to the next source.
when_to_use: Multiple credential sources have defined precedence and an earlier source can be present but expired, revoked, malformed, or otherwise unusable.
Authentication currently chooses the first readable credential rather than the first credential that passes its real verification oracle.
anti_goals: Do not reorder explicit credential precedence, including access-token overrides and the relative priority of local cache versus environment-selected credentials.
Do not accept a credential merely because its file parsed successfully.
Do not remove compute, interactive, or manual authentication paths used after cached candidates are exhausted.
Do not persist compute-provided credentials or broadly redesign the login flow.
not_applicable_when: Only one credential source can exist and there is no supported fallback.
Credential validity can only be established by destructive use with no safe token-acquisition or validation oracle.
The requested behavior is to fail closed on the first configured credential rather than attempt lower-priority sources.
inputs: Source loaders for secure storage and credential files
Token acquisition and server-side validation oracles
Existing override and post-exhaustion authentication behavior
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least two credential sources may be configured, but the resolver exposes only the first loaded credential, so an unusable primary can mask a usable fallback.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Configured candidates are loaded in documented priority order, verified one at a time with the appropriate client, and the first verified candidate is returned; isolated loading or verification failures permit fallback, and existing override and post-exhaustion paths retain their positions.

steps.condition: Run when two or more supported credential sources may coexist or a secure-storage source has a file-based fallback.
steps.validation: Confirm that a valid primary precedes the fallback, a missing or unreadable source does not abort collection, and the environment-selected credential remains present after a parseable primary.

steps.condition: Run for each collected candidate until one verifies or the list is exhausted.
steps.validation: Simulate an expired or revoked first candidate and a valid second candidate; assert that verification continues and the public acquisition call uses the second credential.

validation_ladder: Source-level checks: unreadable, malformed, or absent sources are isolated while valid candidates retain priority order.
Selection checks: a valid primary wins and the fallback is not applied.
Fallback checks: a missing primary selects the secondary source.
Verification-failure regression: an expired or revoked primary is rejected and the valid secondary credential is applied.
Type-adaptation checks: structured application-default credentials use their specialized client while ordinary user credentials use the OAuth client.

Boundary checks: the public memoized client-acquisition entry point returns the selected client, explicit overrides remain first, and compute or interactive authentication remains after candidate exhaustion.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if credential-source precedence cannot be established from implementation or tests.
Stop and reject the workflow if no non-destructive credential verification oracle exists.
Stop when the first verified candidate is found; do not continue into lower-priority credentials.
If every candidate fails, leave control to the repository's existing post-exhaustion authentication path instead of inventing a new recovery mechanism.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, status checks, or recorded test-run result.
The regression test directly proves fallback after ordinary OAuth token-acquisition failure; equivalent failure-path coverage for every structured application-default credential subtype is not shown.
The classifier treats every typed credential except authorized_user as an application-default credential; the complete intended type taxonomy is not documented in the available evidence.

unresolved_questions: Were the focused OAuth tests or the full core test suite executed successfully for f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297? The supplied bundle omits status checks and no execution result was used.

Should typed credentials other than authorized_user always be routed through GoogleAuth.fromJSON? The implementation does so, but the available tests explicitly demonstrate only an external-account case.

Does secure-storage mode intentionally retain GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS as a fallback after an invalid stored credential? The implementation establishes that behavior, but no dedicated regression test for that combination is present.
